_comment: Surface-marker MANO fit for P10, calibrated on P10/static_trial.csv.
Markers are fitted to the MESH SURFACE, not to joint centres: a joint
centre is inside the hand, so the old objective necessarily buried every
attach: marker -> MANO mesh vertex, hand-picked. Physical facts about
this subject's marker placement, so reused unchanged on their movement
trials rather than re-searched per frame. Thumb3 is deliberately NOT
pinned: vertex 708 sits on the middle thumb segment and the automatic
search finds thb-dist correctly (2.71mm vs 7.95mm pinned).
3=IP. This differs from core.correspondence._LABEL_HINTS, which maps
<finger>3 to the fingertip -- unreconciled, see CLAUDE.md.

why_these.staged + freeze_root: fingers drag the root otherwise: palm+MCP alone place the hand to 2.6-6.4mm, but letting fingers vote on orient/transl pushes those same markers to 11-28mm
why_these.min_own_weight 0: a non-zero value moves MCP markers onto finger-dependent skin, which breaks the root stage (it fits them while pose is still at its initial value)
why_these.marker_init: without it the fit converges to a FLAT hand that scores well on the overall mean because 7 of 18 markers are root-determined; with it every joint articulates
why_these.torsion_only: zero axial rotation. Load-bearing, not cosmetic: with torsion free the optimiser satisfies the nailbed marker by twisting instead of flexing, leaving the PIP slack and the MCP over-rotated. Pinning it fixed the index split (PIP 26.6 -> 34.8 against a measured 34.7).
why_these.biomech flexion/abduction bounds: left OFF (--torsion-only). Not yet shown to help; test separately.
why_these.iters_thumb / iters_finger: per-chain stages: with the root frozen each finger is an independent kinematic chain, so fitting them one at a time is mathematically equivalent but differs in optimisation dynamics -- and that matters. FINGERS 9.54 -> 7.95 (thumb stage) -> 6.65 (per-finger), and unlike every other gain this one did NOT drift the joint angles: index1 44.2 against a measured 42.7, index2 34.8 against 34.7.
why_these.iters_root: left at 0 (root_frac). Converging the root fully helps palm+MCP (10.28 -> 8.77mm) but costs the fingers (9.54 -> 10.74) and over-rotates the knuckles: middle1 38.4 -> 57.5 deg against a measured 30.2.
why_these.free_flexion: bound ABDUCTION and torsion, leave flexion free. Flexion genuinely needs range beyond textbook (markers show MCP flexion to 128 deg) and bounding it collapsed the fingers. Abduction does not: p99 is 22-24 deg, at the anatomical limit, but maxima reached 66-100 deg -- the optimiser splaying a finger sideways THROUGH its neighbour to reach a marker (fingertips out of order in 8.8% of frames, index crossing middle in 1.5%). Bounding it IMPROVED everything: fingers 6.65 -> 5.82mm on the pinch window and 20.11 -> 18.86 on the fist window. Same lesson as torsion -- removing a DOF the hand does not have helps rather than costs.
why_these.stretch_gate: flexion-dependent marker slide, applied only above 45 deg. Markers are on the dorsum and the skin there stretches ~20% over a flexing knuckle (correlation +0.80..+0.85, palm control +0.22), which a fixed-vertex attachment cannot follow. Worth 0.9mm near a fist, costs 0.5mm at low flexion where the correction is ~1mm and loses to noise -- hence the gate.

movement_result_fist_window_7930_8130.note: high-flexion poses fit ~3x worse than the pinch window in every configuration tried; this is the dominant remaining error and is not yet explained.
